evidence.paraphrase: The story situates its events in mid-nineteenth-century Alaska during Russian colonial occupation.
evidence.quote: It was in the old days of the Russian occupancy of Alaska, when the nineteenth century had run but half its course, that Negore fled after his fleeing tribe and came upon it this summer night by the head waters of the Pee-lat.

evidence.paraphrase: Russian pursuers are described as intent on exterminating the entire tribe.
evidence.quote: for behind him he knew full well were the dreaded Russians, toiling through the swampy lowlands and over the steep divides, bent on no less than the extermination of all his people.

evidence.paraphrase: The fort at Nulato is destroyed, leaving only ashes and dead men.
evidence.quote: Then I went back to Nulato, and, behold, there was no Nulato fonly ashes where the great fort had stood, and the bodies of many men.

evidence.paraphrase: Negore reads the presence of undisturbed birds as a sign that no ambush lies hidden, using observation to judge whether the way is clear.
evidence.quote: Negore thought of the little birds he had seen perched among the rocks and upon the bushes, and smiled, it was so simple

evidence.paraphrase: Negore infers the presence of a hidden ambush from the absence of birds and a glint of light on a weapon.
evidence.quote: He saw that the little birds were all gone, and once he saw the glint of sunlight on a rifle-barrel.

evidence.paraphrase: The narration explains that Karduk, coming from a treeless sea region, lacks the woodcraft needed to read the signs Negore reads.
evidence.quote: And he was glad that Karduk came from the Great Fog Sea, where there were no trees or bushes, and where men learned water-craft instead of land-craft and wood-craft.

evidence.paraphrase: Members of the tribe mock Negore as a coward.
evidence.quote: fNegore, the Coward, f he heard Illiha, a young woman, laugh, and Sun-ne, his sister fs daughter, laughed with her.

evidence.paraphrase: Negore is shot and experiences the pain of being mortally wounded during the ambush.
evidence.quote: Then he felt torn asunder by a burst of flame hot through his being, and as he fell he knew the sharp pangs of life as it wrenches at the flesh to be free.
